Use it even\\\\n  if they do not mention invocation logging, IAM, service control policies, marketplace subscriptions,\\\\n  chunking, embedding models, vector stores or hybrid search by name. Findings carry LLM-INV and LLM-KB\\\\n  check-ids with a severity and an AWS-doc citation. In every sentence you write, from the first message\\\\n  on and including plans and sub-agent prompts, never write the raw 12-digit account ID and never\\\\n  reproduce retrieved chunk text.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: user-g\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  tier: \\\\\"aws-support-managed\\\\\"\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Reviews Amazon Bedrock setup and Knowledge Bases: invocation logging, model access and lifecycle, denied calls, empty or stale RAG answers and failed ingestion.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"GENERIC\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon Bedrock, AWS IAM, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon S3\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"AI/ML, Security, Governance\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n# OpsAI \\\\u2014 Amazon Bedrock Review\\\\n\\\\nYou review an Amazon Bedrock deployment in two areas and render a posture report with evidence:\\\\n\\\\n- **Model access and configuration** (check family **LLM-INV**): \\\\\"is my Bedrock set up correctly, and\\\\n  can I actually invoke the models I need?\\\\\"\\\\n- **Knowledge bases and RAG** (check family **LLM-KB**): \\\\\"why is my knowledge base returning nothing,\\\\n  stale or wrong answers?\\\\\", telling a knowledge base that merely *exists* from one that is *populated\\\\n  and serving fresh content*.\\\\n\\\\nEvery finding is grounded in a catalog under `references/` with a stable check-id, a severity and an\\\\nAWS-doc citation. You never invent a threshold: where AWS publishes no number the catalog marks it\\\\n`workload-specific` and you report it as `INFO`. This skill uses **read-only APIs only**. It works on\\\\nits own; other skills are optional (see *Related skills (optional)*).\\\\n\\\\n**Output rule \\\\u2014 applies to every sentence you write from the first message on.** Never write the\\\\n12-digit account ID anywhere in text: not in plans, status notes, headings, the Scope line, the final\\\\nanswer, or prompts you give to sub-agents. Write `the account under review` (or its alias). Live runs leaked it in\\\\nlines like \\\\\"The account (`<12 digits>`) is in my enabled associations\\\\\", \\\\\"Account: the account under\\\\nreview (`<12 digits>`)\\\\\", and \\\\\"does not exist in account `<12 digits>`\\\\\". Each of those is a breach,\\\\neven when the user pasted the ID first. The ID belongs only in the tool\\'s `aws_account_id` parameter.\\\\nMask the account segment of every ARN you quote (`arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/...`). No retrieved\\\\nchunk text appears anywhere, even when the user asks for it.\\\\n\\\\n**Answer in this chat.** Run this skill\\'s read-only checks and answer here. Do not stop to offer\\\\nan investigation or to ask whether to keep going, and do not send an interim status line: the first\\\\ntext you send is the finished answer. Ask the user only when an input the checks need is missing (for\\\\nexample which Region or resource), and give what you can answer without it in the same reply.\\\\n\\\\n## Pick the area first\\\\n\\\\nName the area, then read its review file **before the first API call**. Each file holds the router,\\\\nthe step-by-step procedure, the pre-presentation checks, the check family, common wrong answers and\\\\nerror handling for that area.\\\\n\\\\n| The question is about | Area | Read first | Report template |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| Bedrock setup and best practice; invocation logging and its delivery; `AccessDeniedException` or a validation error on `InvokeModel`/`Converse`; model access, marketplace subscription, SCPs; model lifecycle; inference profiles; `InvokeModel` IAM scope; streaming, Converse, batch, `maxTokens`, Prompt Management; throttled model calls | Model access and configuration | `references/model-access-review.md` | `assets/bedrock-configuration-report-template.md` |\\\\n| A knowledge base: empty or stale answers, failed or missing ingestion and sync, chunking, embedding model, data source or vector store encryption and exposure, hybrid search, an unused KB, whether retrieval was ever measured, access denied on ingestion or `Retrieve`, throttling of ingestion or `Retrieve` | Knowledge base and RAG | `references/knowledge-base-review.md` | `assets/rag-health-report-template.md` |\\\\n\\\\nTwo cases that look alike belong to different areas:\\\\n\\\\n- **Access denied.** On `InvokeModel`/`Converse` it is model access (LLM-INV-013/014/015). On an\\\\n  ingestion job or `Retrieve` it is the knowledge base area (LLM-KB-011).\\\\n- **Throttling.** On model invocation it is LLM-INV-007. On ingestion, embedding or `Retrieve` it is\\\\n  LLM-KB-012.\\\\n\\\\nWhen a question spans both areas, run both reviews and present one report with one Scope line: the\\\\nmodel-access section first, then the knowledge base section, each with its own check-ids.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n\\\\nActivate this skill when the user:\\\\n\\\\n- Asks whether their **Bedrock configuration is correct** or set up to best practice.\\\\n- Reports **`AccessDeniedException` on `InvokeModel`**, a model that is **not enabled or access not\\\\n  granted**, a **marketplace subscription** that may never have been accepted, or suspects an **SCP is\\\\n  blocking Bedrock**.\\\\n- Wants to know if **model invocation logging** is enabled, delivering and encrypted.\\\\n- Invokes by a **bare model ID** and asks about **cross-region inference profiles**, or asks whether a\\\\n  **model is deprecated or end-of-life**.\\\\n- Wants **`bedrock:InvokeModel` IAM scope** reviewed, or asks about **streaming vs buffered**,\\\\n  **Converse API**, **batch vs on-demand**, **`maxTokens`** caps or **Prompt Management**.\\\\n- Reports a **knowledge base returning nothing** or with no sources, is poor** (irrelevant chunks, low scores, missed exact matches) or asks\\\\n  what retrieval returns for a query (answered with counts, sources and scores).\\\\n- Asks about **chunking strategy**, whether the **embedding model** is current, **data source or vector\\\\n  store encryption**, **vector store network exposure**, **hybrid vs semantic search**, a knowledge\\\\n  base **not attached to any agent or application**, or **ingestion statistics**.\\\\n- Reports **access denied on ingestion or `Retrieve`** (\\\\\"the KB role can\\'t read my S3 bucket\\\\\",\\\\n  \\\\\"cross-account data source won\\'t sync\\\\\") where the data is intact.\\\\n- Reports **throttling or a quota limit on RAG** (ingestion crawling, `Retrieve` throttled, an\\\\n  embedding quota hit).\\\\n\\\\n## When NOT to Use\\\\n\\\\nThese areas are out of scope. For each, follow *Related skills (optional)*:\\\\n\\\\n- **Guardrail posture**, including contextual-grounding configuration, and **who can call Bedrock**\\\\n  (IAM users and long-lived keys).\\\\n- **Quota and cost posture** (service quotas, Provisioned Throughput sizing, spend, the vector store\\'s\\\\n  bill). Throttling on a specific call path stays here (LLM-INV-007, LLM-KB-012).\\\\n- **Agents and AgentCore** (agent aliases, action groups, runtimes, gateways).\\\\n- **SageMaker** (training, endpoints, scaling, batch, Model Registry).\\\\n- **A live incident**: \\\\\"is this an AWS problem or mine right now?\\\\\" for a failing or slow call.\\\\n- **Model-output quality and running evaluation jobs**, including RAG evaluations. This skill only\\\\n  checks whether a `RagEvaluation` job covers a KB (LLM-KB-009).\\\\n\\\\nWhen a request mixes in-scope and out-of-scope questions, answer the in-scope part in full and never\\\\ngive the out-of-scope part an LLM-INV or LLM-KB check-id.\\\\n\\\\n## Guardrails\\\\n\\\\nNon-negotiable, at every step:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Read-only.** Never call a mutating API. Recommend the fix, state the exact CLI or IaC change and\\\\n   let the user run it. In particular **never call `StartIngestionJob`**: when a sync is the fix, give\\\\n   the command (`aws bedrock-agent start-ingestion-job --knowledge-base-id <kb-id> --data-source-id\\\\n   <ds-id>`). Never attach, put or modify an IAM, bucket, SCP or trust policy, and never call\\\\n   `RequestServiceQuotaIncrease`; return the exact statement or command instead.\\\\n2. **Never echo a raw 12-digit account ID** (Output rule above). Mask the account segment of any ARN\\\\n   quoted as evidence. When you hand work to a sub-agent, put this rule in its prompt.\\\\n3. **Never disclose secret material.** Report env vars, keys, tokens and connection strings by **key\\\\n   name only**, never the value or a partial value.\\\\n4. **Never reproduce retrieved chunk content**, even when asked. Report chunk counts, source\\\\n   identifiers (S3 URIs) and relevance scores, never the chunk text, not even a snippet or excerpt,\\\\n   and say why the text is withheld. A `Retrieve` probe is\\\\n   allowed only as `references/knowledge-base-review.md` defines it (Step 8): at most two queries,\\\\n   `numberOfResults` \\\\u2264 5, content discarded.\\\\n5. **Evidence or silence.** Every finding cites the concrete value that triggered it. Distinguish\\\\n   \\\\\"measured zero\\\\\" from \\\\\"no data reported\\\\\" or \\\\\"no job to read\\\\\" (`references/api-quirks.md` \\\\u00a710).\\\\n6. **A check-id on every finding.** Each finding references an LLM-INV or LLM-KB catalog check-id with\\\\n   that check\\'s severity and AWS-doc citation. No freelance findings.\\\\n7. **Never invent a threshold.** Severities come from the catalogs. No AWS-published number \\\\u2192 `INFO`,\\\\n   marked `workload-specific`.\\\\n8. **Bound the work and disclose what you skipped.** State which Regions, resources, knowledge bases,\\\\n   data sources, steps or checks you did not cover, and why (budget, permissions, a Region without the\\\\n   feature, a focused ask).\\\\n\\\\n## Severity Definitions\\\\n\\\\n| Severity | Meaning | Response SLA (derived) |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| **CRITICAL** | Active production impact or total logging/access blindness. No LLM-KB check carries it | 24\\\\u201348 hours |\\\\n| **HIGH** | Serious reliability, security or least-privilege risk, or retrieval empty or partial | Within 1 week |\\\\n| **MEDIUM** | Meaningful gap vs best practice | Within 30 days |\\\\n| **LOW** | Minor hardening | When convenient |\\\\n| **INFO** | Observation with no AWS-published threshold | N/A \\\\u2014 document / monitor |\\\\n\\\\nSLAs are **derived operational guidance**, not AWS-published commitments. Per-check examples for the\\\\nknowledge base area are in `references/knowledge-base-review.md`.\\\\n\\\\n## Related skills (optional)\\\\n\\\\nThis skill works on its own and loads nothing outside its own `references/` and `assets/`. When a question\\\\nreaches into an area listed under *When NOT to Use*, read `references/related-skills.md` and:\\\\n\\\\n1. If the skill named there is in your available skills, load it and use it for that part.\\\\n2. If it isn\\'t, cover that part yourself with the fallback check in that file and general AWS knowledge.\\\\n   Label anything that comes from general knowledge, and give it no check-id: this skill\\'s check-ids are\\\\n   only for checks this skill runs.\\\\n3. End the answer with one line recommending the missing skill and what it would add. Add it only when\\\\n   that skill would have changed the answer, and only once.\\\\n\\\\n## References\\\\n\\\\n- `references/model-access-review.md`: the model access and configuration review {"id": "fc976418-d77f-401c-9375-ef51827491ae", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_zbzbzJ8hw86IZUvtepZVc7", "content": "[{'text': '# Knowledge base and RAG review (LLM-KB)\\n\\nRead this file before the first API call of a knowledge base or RAG question. Paths are relative to the skill root. The rules in `SKILL.md` (Output rule, Guardrails) apply throughout.\\n\\n## Router\\nHow to read each API and metric is in `references/collection-reference.md`. Load it with any row.\\n\\n| Operator says | First read | Load |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| The knowledge base returns nothing | `ListIngestionJobs` for each data source (empty = never synced), not KB status | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-001), `references/api-quirks.md` |\\n| The ingestion job failed, documents are missing | Latest `GetIngestionJob` `status`, `statistics`, `failureReasons` | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-002) |\\n| RAG answers are out of date, sync is not running | `ListIngestionJobs` recency and sync automation | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-001, LLM-KB-010) |\\n| Which chunking strategy should I use | `GetDataSource` `vectorIngestionConfiguration.chunkingConfiguration` | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-003), `references/api-quirks.md` |\\n| Is my embedding model current | `GetKnowledgeBase` `embeddingModelArn` | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-004) |\\n| Is the data source or vector store encrypted | `GetDataSource` `serverSideEncryptionConfiguration`, the source bucket\\'s `GetBucketEncryption`, and the vector store\\'s own encryption and network policy (the KB response has no encryption key) | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-005, LLM-KB-006) |\\n| Retrieval quality is poor on codes, IDs, SKUs | Retrieval `overrideSearchType` (SEMANTIC vs HYBRID) | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-007) |\\n| Is this knowledge base unused | `ListAgents` \u2192 `ListAgentVersions` \u2192 `ListAgentKnowledgeBases`; application use is unverified unless CloudTrail records KB data events | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-008) |\\n| Has retrieval quality ever been measured | A `RagEvaluation` job whose `ragIdentifiers` include this KB (a `ModelEvaluation` job does not count) | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-009) |\\n| Ingestion or `Retrieve` fails with access denied or not authorized | Latest `GetIngestionJob` `failureReasons`, then `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` on the KB role, the role trust policy (`iam:GetRole`), `s3:GetBucketPolicy`, and SCPs (`organizations:ListPoliciesForTarget`, readable only from the management or a delegated-admin account) | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-011), `references/api-quirks.md` |\\n| Ingestion is slow or `Retrieve` is throttled | `InvocationThrottles` for the embedding model, then `servicequotas:GetServiceQuota` (service-code `bedrock`) | `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-012), `references/api-quirks.md` |\\n| Ingestion or `Retrieve` just started failing, is it AWS or us | `health:DescribeEvents` for an active Bedrock event in the region, before any customer fix | `references/collection-reference.md` (transient-vs-config classifier), `references/checks-rag-knowledgebase.md` (LLM-KB-011, LLM-KB-012) |\\n| Vector-store or retrieval metric looks like zero | `AWS/AOSS` and retrieval signals, no-datapoints vs measured zero | `references/metrics-and-logs.md` |\\n\\n## The RAG Health Review\\nThis is the main procedure. The exact calls, fields and decision rules for every step are in\\n`references/rag-review-playbook.md`; follow it. Where it is more specific than a shared reference, the\\nplaybook governs.\\n\\nFor a **full review**, run all ten steps in order. For a **focused question**, run the steps it needs\\nplus Steps 1\u20132 (they identify the KB and data sources), and list the steps you did not run under\\n**Scope not covered**. Never present a conclusion from a step you did not run.\\n\\n- [ ] Step 1: `ListKnowledgeBases`, then `GetKnowledgeBase` for embedding model and `storageConfiguration` (store type and id). The KB response has no encryption key.\\n- [ ] Step 2: `ListDataSources`, then `GetDataSource` for `chunkingConfiguration`, `serverSideEncryptionConfiguration`, bucket and inclusion prefixes.\\n- [ ] Step 3: `ListIngestionJobs` sorted `STARTED_AT` `DESCENDING`, all pages. An **empty list means never synced** (LLM-KB-001, HIGH).\\n- [ ] Step 4: For the latest terminal job (`COMPLETE` / `FAILED` / `STOPPED`), read `status`, the `numberOf\u2026` statistics and `failureReasons` (LLM-KB-002).\\n    - **Service-vs-customer transient verdict first.** On a `FAILED` ingestion job, before prescribing any customer fix, decide whether the fault is **service-side** (regional capacity / a Bedrock service event \u2014 check `health:DescribeEvents` for an active event in the region) or **customer-side** (config / permissions / quota). Only prescribe a customer fix once a service event is ruled out; if a service event is active, report it as transient and advise retry rather than a config change.\\n    - If `failureReasons` indicate an **access/authorization** denial (not a data problem), run **LLM-KB-011** (simulate the execution role, inspect trust/bucket policy and SCPs) and return the exact missing statement.\\n    - If ingestion is **slow or throttled** rather than a hard data failure, run **LLM-KB-012**: `servicequotas:GetServiceQuota` (service-code `bedrock`) for the embedding-model invocation / KB quotas and correlate CloudWatch `InvocationThrottles` / `EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage` over the window; report `workload-specific`/`INFO` where AWS publishes no number.\\n- [ ] Step 5: Decide **populated** from a `COMPLETE` job with `numberOfNewDocumentsIndexed` > 0. A later no-change sync (0 new, 0 modified) is not emptiness. If populated but answers have no sources, follow the playbook\\'s candidate-cause table; never diagnose by elimination.\\n- [ ] Step 6: Chunking (LLM-KB-003), embedding-model currency (LLM-KB-004), and staleness: newest S3 `LastModified` under the prefix vs the latest `COMPLETE` job\\'s `updatedAt`.\\n- [ ] Step 7: Encryption of the data source and transient storage (LLM-KB-005) and of the vector store, plus its network policy (LLM-KB-006). Keep field absent / AWS-owned key / CMK apart. Access & authorization (LLM-KB-011) when ingestion or `Retrieve` is denied: `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` on the KB / data-source execution role for `s3:GetObject` / `s3:ListBucket` and `kms:Decrypt`, the role trust policy for `bedrock.amazonaws.com`, and `s3:GetBucketPolicy` for a cross-account bucket policy; SCP reads (`organizations:ListPoliciesForTarget` / `DescribePolicy`) work only from the management or a delegated-admin account. On a denial, return the exact missing statement with the account segment masked.\\n- [ ] Step 8: Search type (LLM-KB-007, INFO) and, only if needed and allowed, one bounded `Retrieve` probe (counts, URIs, scores).\\n    - If a `Retrieve` / `RetrieveAndGenerate` call (the probe or the user\\'s) fails or is throttled, apply the **service-vs-customer transient verdict** first (`health:DescribeEvents` for an active Bedrock event in the Region), then classify: `AccessDenied` \u2192 **LLM-KB-011**; `ThrottlingException` or quota pressure on retrieval or the embedding model \u2192 **LLM-KB-012**. Report chunk counts, sources and scores only, never chunk content.\\n- [ ] Step 9: `ListAgents` \u2192 `ListAgentVersions` \u2192 `ListAgentKnowledgeBases`, and whether CloudTrail records KB data events (LLM-KB-008).\\n- [ ] Step 10: Sync automation (LLM-KB-010, INFO) and whether a `RagEvaluation` job covers this KB (LLM-KB-009); running the evaluation is output-quality work (follow *Related skills (optional)* in `SKILL.md`).\\n\\n**Always land a result in a single turn.** Each step is best-effort: if an API is denied, a list is\\nempty for an unknown reason, or a region does not support a feature, record that signal as\\n`unavailable` or `not checked` and move on. - For frequent small changes, use direct document ingestion (`IngestKnowledgeBaseDocuments`) instead of full syncs. Keep the S3 sync for bulk loads.
- Split very large corpora across several KBs so jobs can run in parallel.
- If the slow job is a first-time bulk load, check the vector store's write capacity as well. I haven't looked at it.

## What I couldn't verify
- Your actual slow KB and Region. Which KB ID, and which Region, is the one that's crawling?

- The quota listing was truncated, and the Cohere embed tokens-per-minute value wasn't seen.
